overview: Ludwig van Beethoven was a composer and pianist from Bonn who made his career in Vienna, where he earned an early reputation as a pianist and improviser. As his hearing deteriorated, he kept composing, writing piano sonatas, string quartets and symphonies that stretched the musical forms he had inherited.

keyMoments.title: From Bonn to Vienna
keyMoments.text: Beethoven moved from Bonn to Vienna, where he studied composition with **Joseph Haydn**. He gained an early reputation there for playing and improvising at the piano.

keyMoments.title: A letter kept private
keyMoments.text: At **Heiligenstadt** outside Vienna, Beethoven wrote a letter intended for his brothers. In it he described his despair over his worsening hearing. He described suicidal thoughts and a renewed resolve to keep composing. The letter stayed among his papers and was discovered after his death.

keyMoments.title: The Eroica at the Theater an der Wien
keyMoments.text: Vienna's **Theater an der Wien** hosted a public performance of Beethoven's **Third Symphony**. The work was unusually long for a symphony of its time. Its second movement is a funeral march, and the symphony is known as the Eroica, or heroic symphony.

keyMoments.title: Voices enter the Ninth
keyMoments.text: An orchestra performed Beethoven's **Ninth Symphony** in Vienna. The first three movements were entirely instrumental. Then solo singers and a choir joined the orchestra for the finale, singing words from **Friedrich Schiller's** poem Ode to Joy.

deepFacts.text: As Beethoven's hearing declined, visitors could talk to him by writing their remarks in notebooks. Some of these conversation books survive.
Beethoven wrote 33 piano variations on a single waltz by the publisher Anton Diabelli. The complete set is known as the **Diabelli Variations**.
